articles.title: "Me sorprende que no esté todavía en la UFC"
articles.standfirst: Beneil Dariush ha alabado la figura de Usman Nurmagomedov, cuyo fichaje por la compañía se podría anunciar próximamente
articles.summary: Beneil Dariush ha alabado la figura de Usman Nurmagomedov, cuyo fichaje por la compañía se podría anunciar próximamente
articles.body: Usman Nurmagomedov es agente libre desde hace unos días, una vez acabaron los 90 días de plazo que tenía PFL para intentar renovar el contrato de su campeón de peso ligero y número uno libra por libra. Por tanto, el fichaje del primo de Khabib Nurmagomedov por la compañía dirigida por Dana White podría ser inminente, aunque todo un veterano como Beneil Dariush se ha mostrado sorprendido de que no esté en la promotora desde antes. Hace no tanto, Dariush llegó a estar bien posicionado para enfrentarse a Islam Makhachev por el cinturón de peso liger, aunque en sus últimos combates ha sido finalizado por rivales como Benoit Saint-Denis o Quillan Salkilld y ha quedado en un segundo plano. Aún así, su voz es una de las más autorizadas de la división, y ha alabado la figura de Usman. "Me sorprende que aún no esté en la UFC. Es tan fuerte que supongo que el motivo tiene que ver con algún asunto relacionado con el contrato. Es realmente muy, muy fuerte. Creo que se enfrentará directamente a un peleador del top 10", afirmó Dariush en una entrevista con MMA Junkie. Razón no le falta, ya que en caso de que Usman acabe recalando en la UFC lo normal es que le enfrenten directamente con un peleador del top de la categoría. Nurmagomedov había pedido incluso el cinturón, aunque primero tendrá que tener una prueba de fuego para ver en qué nivel se encuentra realmente, ya que han habido casos anteriores en los que estos fichajes no han salido bien. Por mucho que venga como una superestrella, hay ejemplos como los de Patchy Mix, Kai Asakura, Patricio Pitbull o Michael Chandler que ponen en evidencia que la UFC es otro nivel. Es cierto que el caso de Usman es diferente, ya que llega muy joven, siendo el mejor peleador de PFL y uno de los bastiones más importantes del 'Team Khabib', pero hay que ir con pies de plomo. Lo que sí ha hecho muy bien es hablar y darse a conocer, teniendo ciertos piques con Ilia Topuria y algunos otros nombres de la organización para ir forjando rivalidades que vendan mejor sus posibles combates en un futuro. Además, al contrario que Makhachev o Khabib, Usman basa su estilo más en el striking, por lo que será muy interesante ver cómo se integran sus habilidades en una de las categorías más importantes y competitivas de la UFC.

images.caption: Usman Nurmagomedov, tras ganar a Alfie Davis en PFL Dubái. PFL.

articles.title: Ex-boxing champion Deontay Wilder returns to co-headline Fury vs. Joshua
articles.summary: The Tyson Fury vs. Anthony Joshua card just got bigger.
articles.body:
The Tyson Fury vs. Anthony Joshua card just got bigger.

Former WBC heavyweight champion Deontay Wilder is set to compete in the co-main event Dec. 11 card at Principality Stadium in Cardiff, Wales. Wilder, one of the biggest heavyweight stars of this generation, takes on Zuffa Boxing cruiserweight champion Jai Opetaia.

Wilder (45-4-1), who had two massive title fights with Fury in 2020 and 2021, looks to continue building momentum off the back of two consecutive victories against Tyrrell Anthony Herndon in 2025 and Derek Chisora this past April. Since losing his WBC title to Fury in their pair of fights, Wilder has gone 3-2.

Opetaia (31-0) looks to capitalize on easily the biggest name he's ever faced in his boxing career. For this opportunity, Opetaia moves up a weight class from cruiserweight to heavyweight. The Australian fighter last competed in September when he defended his Zuffa Boxing title against Noel Mikaelian.

articles.title: Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua: Deontay Wilder vs Jai Opetaia added to undercard in Cardiff
articles.summary: American Deontay Wilder will fight Australia's Jai Opetaia on the undercard of Tyson Fury v Anthony Joshua in December at Cardiff's Principality Stadium.
articles.body:
American Deontay Wilder will fight Australia's Jai Opetaia on the undercard of Tyson Fury v Anthony Joshua in December.

The bout will serve as the co-main event for the long-awaited all-British heavyweight fight, with the WBA 'super' heavyweight title on the line at Cardiff's Principality Stadium.

Unbeaten WBA 'regular' cruiserweight champion Opetaia, 31, will step up to heavyweight for the first time to fight Wilder, a former world champion with 43 knockouts.

Wilder (45-4-1, 43 KOs) will hope to re-establish himself among the heavyweight elite, while Opetaia (31-0, 24 KOs) could be eyeing a fresh challenge, after years of dominance at cruiserweight.

Wilder, 41, held the WBC heavyweight title from 2015 to 2020 and is regarded as one of the most feared punchers of his generation.

The American also enjoyed an epic trilogy with Fury, but came out on the losing side with a draw and two defeats.

Wilder had also been close to facing Joshua but a knockout loss against China's Zhilei Zhang in June 2024 derailed the potential bout.

Tickets for the main event sold out in under an hour, despite the ringwalks being expected to start around 01:00 GMT on Saturday, 12 December, following a short live music performance, and the stadium will remain open until 03:30.

The remaining bouts on the undercard are still to be announced, with Wales' former IBF super-featherweight champion Joe Cordina thought to be in negotiations to fight Manny Pacquiao.

Why is cruiserweight champion Opetaia fighting heavyweight Wilder?

This will be a first high-level heavyweight fight for Opetaia, who is a previous holder of the IBF championship and a force at cruiserweight.

A move to Zuffa Boxing has brought complications for the Australian - who stopped WBC champion Noel Mikaelian in September but could not claim his belt due to a sanctioning dispute.

Opetaia faced off against David Benavidez after his victory over Mikaelian and a future cruiserweight fight could still happen if the Mexican comes through his three-belt unification bout with Michal Cieslak.

For Wilder, this presents a chance to be the first professional boxer to get the better of Opetaia.

Wilder has lost two of his previous four fights, but picked up a win last time out with a split-decision win over Briton Derek Chisora in April.

images.caption: Image caption, Deontay Wilder is almost 10 years older than Jai Opetaia

articles.title: Joshua Buatsi 'open' to potential world title rematch with Zach Parker, if he beats dangerous puncher Umar Dzambekov
articles.summary: Joshua Buatsi edged out Zack Parker in a tight contest last year but is open to a rematch, potentially for a world title; Parker must beat dangerous Umar Dzambekov; Watch Parker vs Dzambekov live on Sky Sports' digital platforms from 5pm on Saturday
articles.body:
Parker, a high-level operator, meets the dangerous Austrian at the Copper Box Arena on Saturday.

Dzambekov has dazzled with sensational one-punch knockouts and his clash with Parker could be a thriller. Watch it live on Sky Sports ' digital platforms early on Saturday evening.

Later that night Buatsi rematches Willie Hutchinson for the vacant WBC light-heavyweight world championship.

Parker still disputes his points reversal to Buatsi last year. "Every man and his dog walking down the street, the first thing they say to me is you defo won the Buatsi fight. I think it's just plain to see if you got eyes," he told Sky Sports .

"I'm not that bitter anymore," Parker added. "You've got to take your ups and downs.

"I've got a big fight in front of me, it's probably a harder fight than the Buatsi fight.

Buatsi told Sky Sports : "The Zach Parker one, it's still a good opponent but what I couldn't comprehend was being on the floor and thinking you won the fight. It was a spoiler of a style.

"I'm not telling you how to box or what tactics to use but simply being on the canvas so many times and thinking that's going to give you a win, it doesn't make sense."

He is however open to a rematch with Parker if they both come through their next fights victorious.

"I've always been open to fighting these guys and taking these fights," Buasti said. "Let him do what he's got to do. First and foremost I have to handle business."

He is expecting to repeat a victory over Hutchinson and win the WBC belt. "It's been a whole career waiting for this opportunity," Buatsi said. "To now be fighting for a full world title, it's all I've been training for for many years.

"I'm simply expecting a better version to the guy that I boxed two years ago. He's had two fights since and so have I, I've boxed better opposition I would definitely say.

"I'm expecting a better Hutchinson. He is a good fighter."

Parker has a skilled, dangerous opponent to contend with himself at the Copper Box. But it's a bout he didn't hesitate to take.

"This is the boxing game," he said. "Put them in front of me and I'll go out and beat them.

"I'm like the old-school boxers. This is my job. I've got to go out do my job no matter who's in front of me."

Watch Parker vs Dzambekov live on Sky Sports' digital platforms from 5pm on Saturday.

articles.title: UFC owners discuss expansion onto HBO, other platforms under Paramount-Warner Bros. partnership
articles.summary: The UFC won’t just stay on Paramount+ forever it seems
articles.body:
You might catch a UFC special on HBO sooner rather than later.

Paramount-Skydance recently closed a massive $110 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. and all of the company's assets, including networks like HBO, TBS, TNT, and many others. While the UFC's broadcast deal with Paramount that kicked off at the start of 2026 landed the majority of the organization's programming on the Paramount+ streaming service, this merger opens the door to all sorts of possibilities.

TKO Group Holdings president and COO Mark Shapiro revealed on Wednesday that talks are already ongoing about the merger and the UFC's potential expansion to different networks.

"We're in conversation as we speak with Skydance about the best way to maximize audience across the Skydance platform," Shapiro said during a TKO financial call. "We have a great partnership with the entire team there. I used to work with David Berson, who's the head of Skydance Sports, from our days at ESPN. He's super creative.

"We will be maximizing HBO, TNT, Paramount+, CBS, all in the name of expanding eyeballs, expanding viewership, growing audience, and increasing engagement. Fully aligned strategically with Skydance and, frankly, they made a huge investment in UFC, and we want to see that we help them maximize their returns."

The UFC inked a huge seven-year, $7.7 billion deal to move from ESPN to Paramount at the start of 2026 while simultaneously eliminating pay-per-view broadcasts, with every event now airing exclusively on the Paramount+ streaming service.

While the merger between Paramount and Warner Bros. is complete, the full integration for all the various properties is still underway. Eventually, Paramount+ is expected to merge with HBO Max, and that immediately increases overall subscriptions and viewership.

There's no telling how much Paramount plans to feature the UFC on the different platforms, but obviously it sounds like that kind of programming could be happening in the near future.

articles.title: AEW Dynamite Results, Winners, Live Grades, Reaction, Highlights From Blood & Guts 2026
articles.summary: Welcome to Bleacher Report's coverage of the Blood and Guts episode of Dynamite on November 4.
articles.body:
Welcome to Bleacher Report's coverage of the Blood and Guts episode of Dynamite on November 4.

This year's event featured two B&G matches, one for the men's division and one for the women's division.

Will Ospreay led a team against The Don Callis Family, and Willow Nightingale led a team of babyfaces against The Triangle of Madness, Divine Dominion and Persephone.

Let's take a look at what happened at this year's Blood and Guts event.

Renee Paquette interviewed Don Callis and the DCF backstage after Excalibur welcomed us to the show. Callis promised to do a lot of damage heading into Full Gear, which will set up Kyle Fletcher, Mark Davis and Jake Doyle to win gold. We also heard from Will Ospreay's team in a separate interview.

The women's Blood and Guts match got the action started. Megan Bayne was the first entrant for her team. Their team won the coin flip to earn the advantage, so Kris Statlander was going to be outnumbered when the third woman entered the ring. Here is the order of entry for everyone:

Bayne was the first to lose any blood, and it was quite a bit. She was a crimson mess after the first commercial break. Blue was busted open before she even got into the ring, and with all-white gear, the red stood out as she got bloodier.

This match was exactly as advertised. It was absolute mayhem from start to finish. There wasn't a single woman of the 12 who competed who came away from this match without a few cuts and bruises. Even the ones who were not covered in blood will feel this match for days.

Whether you like this or not is going to come down to personal preference. It's not a traditional wrestling match, so it shouldn't be judged like one. This bout was trying to be something different, more violent, and in that regard, it succeeded.

AEW has created a handful of signature matches over the years, but Blood and Guts stands out for the sheer brutality it delivers every single time. The effort these 12 women put into this performance was incredible.

This match took up almost the entire first hour of the show. The babyfaces ended up winning after Hart was forced to tap out to a submission from both Statlander and Cameron, which included some barbed wire wrapped around her face.

Result: Statlander, Cameron, Hayter, Windsor, Nightingale and Aminata won

If you watch the show on HBO Max, that music that plays before it starts really lulls you into a false sense of security before Dynamite comes blaring in with Excalibur excitedly screaming.

Adam Copeland told Mick Foley that he was wearing the same gear that he wore for their match that was so iconic.

Stat and Bayne both brought weapons into the ring, but neither one used them to start.

Persephone brought a briefcase into the ring that contained some of Britt Baker's dental equipment. She tried to use some dental forceps on Statlander.

Blue used a few light tubes that were taped together to hit Statlander as she came to the ring.

Cameron brought two guitars into the ring. Kross broke the first one, so Harley hit her with the second one, which was full of some kind of powder that went everywhere.

Hayter broke a bunch of bottles over the heads of her opponents.

Statlander fell between the cage and apron after taking a powerbomb. It looked painful.

Austin Creed was shown questioning Swerve Strickland about attacking Bandido last week without consulting them. Off in the distance, Kofi could be heard screaming in pain. Bandido was revealed to be the attacker when he took out Creed, and he started brawling with Swerve.

Hangman and Brody King showed up to even the score. Bandido told them he wants to take Swerve's life after what he did last week. They finally agreed to the Texas Death match at Full Gear.

This was a good way to fill some time between the two Blood and Guts matches while simultaneously confirming another match for the upcoming PPV.

Bandido, having just as much of a reason to hate Swerve as Hangman has, is going to make this even more interesting to watch unfold in the coming weeks.

Creed Speared Bandido to prevent him from using part of the stage as a weapon, but the piece of metal still ended up falling and hitting Swerve in the head unexpectedly.

Seeing Creed and Kofi in a Texas Death match after they spent so long working in a PG environment is going to be very entertaining.

Mercedes Mone had a segment calling out Marina Shafir so she could talk some trash ahead of their title match. They ended up getting into a fight that The CEO barely managed to win. We also got a promo from Nick Wayne.

The men's Blood and Guts match took place during the second hour of the show. One side was entirely made up of members of The Don Callis Family, while the other side was a group of people who do not always see eye to eye but set aside their differences for a common goal.

The Don Callis Family had the advantage after the coin flip. Here is the order of entry:

Throughout most of the match, it felt like the men were relying on weapons a lot less than the women, so this bout didn't quite reach the same level of chaos as early as the women did.

The pacing of the entrances and order of participants felt right. Having Fletcher begin the match while Ospreay came out last for his team was an interesting juxtaposition. You would usually expect those roles to be flipped with the heel and babyface.

The thing this bout did very effectively was showcasing the feud between Ospreay and Fletcher. They were not the only storyline in this match, but it felt like the most important one.

The final third of this match was definitely the best part. We saw weapons, explosions and bumps galore. Much like with the women, not a single person left this match unscathed.

It felt like all 12 guys had their own individual moments, which is not always an easy thing to do in a bout like this. Fletcher had Copeland tied up and gave him a mic. They forced him to surrender the match to prevent Fletcher from using a screwdriver on Ospreay's neck.

The match was over, but the carnage was not. Wardlow sent Allin flying off the top of the cage through a bunch of tables that were set up on the floor.

The Conglomeration and Jon Moxley had a segment that showed them appearing to join forces to take on The Cut.

Having Borden in a match like this so early in his career was a risky move for AEW.

Mercedes might not have been competing, but her outfit was covered in blood-stained designs anyway.

Allin and Borden had a special entrance video before Allin came to the ring. He also ran the NYC marathon on Friday with almost no preparation.

Allin was the first man to bleed, which is the least surprising sentence in this entire recap.

Copeland brought a chair with him and hit everyone on the opposing team as the crowd continued to sing his music.

The way Doyle and Davis threw Allin into the cage wall was bonkers.

Okada used a leaf blower to get rid of the thumbtacks in the ring.

Knight's coast to coast dropkick into a barbed wire chair was awesome.

Wardlow falling for Allin's trapped backpack while everyone else knew to be scared of it was hilarious.

Report: Raiders Sending Jeanty 'Wake-Up Call' ⏰

With the exception of a few random interviews and segments, and two short fights, the entire show was taken up by the two Blood and Guts matches.

Both bouts featured some wild moments, a lot of blood, and some storyline developments as AEW gets closer to Full Gear.

The women's Blood and Guts match outperformed the men's by a slight margin, but the most brutal thing we saw all night happened in the men's match when Allin was thrown off the cage through some tables.

Even though it was just two matches, we got to see 24 men and women go to battle inside the cage. It was a great night of action, especially for those of you who like the more violent side of AEW.

articles.title: Chris Billam-Smith versus Oleksandr Usyk? 'Not next... Maybe if he beats David Benavidez and I beat Jai Opetaia!'
articles.summary: Oleksandr Usyk's potential return to cruiserweight would add a whole new dimension to the division; Chris Billam-Smith believes, with Usyk likely to fight David Benavidez, he can target Jai Opetaia once again; But Billam-Smith has a dangerous clash with Cheavon Clarke this Saturday first
articles.body:
Usyk was an undisputed world champion at cruiserweight before he repeated that feat twice over at heavyweight, beating Tyson Fury, Anthony Joshua and Daniel Dubois among others.

But the great Ukrainian's team has revealed that he is now considering returning to cruiserweight before the end of his career .

It's a move the Billam-Smith, the former WBO cruiserweight world champion, welcomes.

"Probably it's fair to say it knocks me down a spot in the world rankings!" he told Sky Sports .

"But it's also great for the division, a huge name for the division that really probably has been the face of boxing, definitely in terms of achievement."

Usyk would be expected to target formidable cruiserweight champion David Benavidez, the current WBA and WBO titlist.

If Benavidez does box Usyk, it means he won't be fighting Jai Opetaia, another elite cruiserweight, next. Opetaia would still most likely return to cruiserweight after his December clash with Deontay Wilder but then he will be looking for an opponent himself.

That would be Billam-Smith's opportunity. He is still gunning for that fight.

"That definitely seems more doable now," he said. "I'm happy about that, because I think Benavidez would beat him and I always wanted to be the first man to beat Opetaia."

If Usyk wanted to re-accustom himself to boxing at cruiserweight before fighting Benavidez he could do worse than selecting a strong, come-forward, former world champion like Billam-Smith in an interim bout.

But Billam-Smith would expect Usyk to go straight into a fight with Benavidez, even though the Ukrainian hasn't fought since beating Rico Verhoeven in May.

"I think the level he's been and the level he's at in terms of marketable fights, I think he'd go straight into a Benavidez fight, especially at his age now," Billam-Smith said, before adding with a laugh: "I think taking interim fight, especially dangerous ones, against me, he doesn't need to be doing."

But Billam-Smith can dare to dream. On Saturday, live on Sky Sports , he fights Cheavon Clarke. Win that and it could be Opetaia next. Win that and he'd be right at the summit of the division. Then why couldn't an Usyk fight happen?

"Not next, maybe if he beats Benavidez, I beat Opetaia, that's a nice little southpaw to warm up with before I go in with Usyk," he said cheerfully.

Why is Usyk risking his legacy by making a potentially perilous return to the cruiserweight division? "Challenge. Purely challenge," Viddal Riley, the European cruiserweight champion, told Sky Sports .

"He keeps hearing: 'This guy's a monster, this guy's a monster' and then there's a part of him that just wants to show people: no, he's not a monster. I'm the guy. I've always been the guy.

"I think it's a lot of ego involved and it could backfire. It could backfire. People don't really go to heavyweight, come back down and look the same.

"I don't like to see the greats and the OGs do things like that because you're letting the goalposts move and trying to keep up when you've achieved everything you need to achieve.

"But it's still good for me and the division because we get spoken about more."

Watch Chris Billam-Smith vs Cheavon Clarke this Saturday live on Sky Sports .

articles.title: Ilia Topuria Gets Major UFC Return Update From Dana White
articles.summary: Dana White recently said that Ilia Topuria could make his UFC return as early as Q1 of 2027.
articles.body:
Fans have been eagerly waiting for Ilia Topuria to return to the Octagon. As things stand, it has been nearly five months since the Spaniard was stopped at UFC Freedom 250 in June. The former two-division champion took so much damage that his corner had to pull him out of the fight on the stool after the fourth round.

Topuria suffered two broken orbital bones, a cracked septum, and a shattered foot. However, despite the severity of his injuries , he has already returned to social media and resumed training ahead of his next outing.

Footage of him working on his striking alongside boxers like Lasha Guruli in his native Georgia has given fans a glimpse of his recovery. More recently, he even visited the iconic Didgori Battle Memorial on Mount Didgori, a site that stands as a symbol of Georgian resilience and victory.

Amid all this, Dana White has finally offered an update on Topuria's potential UFC return. During a recent appearance on The Jim Rome Show, the UFC CEO told the host that the former champion could be back in early 2027.

He said, "In 2027. He'll come back in early 2027. We're working on that, too. That entire lightweight division, you've got Gaethje, Topuria, Arman Tsarukyan, Oliveira, Paddy Pimblett, Holloway. The whole top 10 is straight killers and the most badass division we have right now."

While White didn't reveal who could welcome the Spaniard back to the Octagon, Topuria's camp has been pushing for an immediate rematch with Justin Gaethje for the lightweight title.

However, with the American's future still uncertain , Gaethje could potentially vacate the belt. If that happens, Topuria could find himself facing Arman Tsarukyan for the vacant gold.

Paddy Pimblett is another name in the mix. The Englishman has called out Topuria for a grudge match by suggesting a season of The Ultimate Fighter. The proposed matchup would finally settle their long-running rivalry, which dates back to 2022 .

With White pointing toward early 2027, fans could potentially see Topuria make his return at UFC 337, UFC 338, or UFC 339. Those events are expected to take place in February, March, and April 2027, respectively.

articles.title: Billam-Smith vs Clarke: Amateur rivalry renewed
articles.summary: Former crusierweight world champion Chris Billam-Smith is hoping to get one over his old amateur rival Cheavon Clarke when the two meet on Saturday at London’s Copper Box Arena.
articles.body:
Good things come to those who wait - or so hopes Chris Billam-Smith.

On Saturday, he gets the opportunity to end a 10-year wait for revenge when he shares a ring with Cheavon Clarke at London's Copper Box.

The Britons boxed in the final of the 2016 National Championships, with Clarke winning by decision.

"Any competitor is going to want to get one back on someone," he told BBC Sport.

"It wasn't a fight I was chasing but the fact I get the chance is just an added bonus and I think it's a great opportunity for me to do that for my younger self if nothing else."

Clarke, 35, went on to enjoy a successful amateur career, fighting at both the Commonwealth and Olympic Games, while Billam-Smith had to wait until the professional ranks to flourish.

After entering the professional ranks in 2017, Billam-Smith, 36, won British and European titles before his crowning moment of becoming cruiserweight world champion in 2023 .

"It's a message really that it's not where you start, it's how you finish and I think that I get to prove the progress I've made over the last 10 years on Saturday night."

Billam-Smith has lost twice in 22 fights as a professional and enjoyed an 18-month stint as WBO cruiserweight world champion.

His reign came to an end when attempting to unify against WBA 'super' champion Gilberto Ramirez in November 2024, but Billam-Smith maintains an ambition to return to the highest level.

After bouncing back to beat Brandon Glanton in April 2025, Billam-Smith signed with Zuffa Boxing and stopped Ryan Rozicki on his debut in June.

Billam-Smith's decision to join the Zuffa Boxing ranks was partly motivated by the possibility of facing WBA 'regular' champion Jai Opetaia.

Australia's Opetaia, who also moved to the promotion in January, has been a long-term target for the Englishman.

Hopes of earning a shot at the 31-year-old appear more distant than ever, though, with Opetaia moving up to heavyweight to face Deontay Wilder on the Tyson Fury v Anthony Joshua undercard on 11 December.

"Opetaia is facing Deontay Wilder in December or David Benavidez in May so who knows, but it's a fight that makes sense with us both being at Zuffa," Billam-Smith said.

"We all know how boxing works so it isn't as easy as win this one and then fight him. If it doesn't materialise then I'll just carry on my career as I have done.

"Our timelines just haven't really matched up yet. If he fights Benavidez then to be honest I think Benavidez beats him so then that fight would be sort of dead in the water from my point of view, we'll see."

images.caption: Image caption, Clarke beat Billam-Smith in the 2016 National Championships final

articles.title: Dana White: "Ilia Topuria volverá a principios de 2027"
articles.standfirst: El 'Matador' aún no tiene combate anunciado
articles.summary: El 'Matador' aún no tiene combate anunciado
articles.body: Si ya avisó Ilia Topuria (17-1) con que estaba de vuelta, ahora sido la UFC la que ha confirmado, a través de Dana White, que el retorno del 'Matador' debería producirse a principios de 2027. El ex campeón del peso ligero y también monarca en el peso pluma sigue recuperándose de su derrota ante Justin Gaethje (28-5) en UFC Casa Blanca pero ya se trabaja en su regreso. "En 2027. Volverá a principios de 2027, estamos trabajando en eso", confirmó Dana White en una entrevista en el programa de Jim Rome al ser preguntado por Ilia Topuria. El 'boss' de la UFC confirmó que está tremendamente ilusionado por el futuro de la división del peso ligero, nombrándola como la más dura de toda la UFC, y mencionando nombres como Gaethje, el propio Topuria, Tsarukyan, Oliveira, Pimblett o Max Holloway. Ilia, mientras, sigue en Georgia, donde lleva ya más de un mes completando su recuperación. "Volví al lugar donde todo empezó. No para rememorar el pasado, sino para recordar. Vuelve el Matador", escribía estos días en su cuenta de Instagram. Está por ver, sin embargo, la 'precisión' de las palabras de Dana White... pues un retorno de Topuria en enero ya es imposible (UFC 336 se ha anunciado, y no está), y con "principios de 2027" la horquilla es bastante amplia. Como ya comentamos en MARCA, todo apunta a una fecha pasado el mes de marzo.

images.caption: Ilia Topuria y Dana White, en Whasington. UFC.

articles.title: Davey Grant: UFC's longest-serving Briton relishing life in the octagon at 40
articles.summary: The UFC's longest-serving Briton Davey Grant says his time in the promotion has been "the best portion of my life".
articles.body:
The UFC's longest-serving Briton Davey Grant says his time in the promotion has been "the best portion of my life".

The 40-year-old is set to fight American bantamweight Elijah Smith in Las Vegas on Saturday, almost 13 years after debuting in the UFC.

Although fighters such as Michael Bisping and Leon Edwards have fought more times in the UFC, no Briton has ever been in the promotion for longer.

Grant made his UFC debut in November 2013 and has fought 16 times in the promotion, winning nine.

"What a ride – it's been the best portion of my life," said Grant.

"I'm so grateful to still be doing this. I thank my lucky stars, I've lived the life I've wanted to live and I'm so thankful to still be here and doing what I love."

Smith's father Gilbert fought in the UFC only seven months before Grant debuted in the promotion.

Aged 24, Smith is 16 years younger than Grant and has won all three of his UFC fights after debuting in the organisation last year.

Grant is undeterred by his younger opponent and says his skills have improved with age.

Grant, who's from Darlington but has moved to Las Vegas with his wife and children, beams as he reveals the motivation behind his enduring career.

"Everything I do is for the family. I'm a father first, then I'm a husband, then I'm a fighter," said Grant.

"Doing well in fighting helps me do those. As well as that I just love it so much, I don't want it to stop.

"The harder I train, the better I do in fights, the healthier I keep myself, I'll get to keep doing what I love."

Grant has suffered multiple injuries during his UFC tenure which means his 16 fights in the promotion is fewer than Bisping's 29 and Edwards' 19.

He has given no indication his fight against Smith will be his last, but says he is looking forward to retirement.

"Just because I don't want to retire it doesn't mean I'm not looking forward to it and I won't absolutely enjoy it," said Grant.

"No matter what happens I'm living the live I could only ever have dreamed of."

articles.title: Alycia Baumgardner predicts she will 'easily pick apart' Caroline Dubois if fighters meet next year
articles.summary: Unified super-featherweight world champion Alycia Baumgardner steps up to lightweight to take on unbeaten IBF champion Elif Nur Turhan, live on Sky Sports from 1.30am on Monday; Baumgardner feels she is No 1 women's boxer, calls Nur Turhan "one-way fighter"
articles.body:
American Baumgardner, the unified super-featherweight world champion, will step up to lightweight to take on unbeaten IBF champion Elif Nur Turhan in Texas on Sunday night (Monday morning UK), live on Sky Sports .

British star Dubois is the WBC and WBO lightweight champion and is looking for a potential blockbuster showdown with Baumgardner in 2027.

Dubois branded Baumgardner a "coward" after the two feistily exchanged words following unbeaten Dubois' win over Amelia Moore in Birmingham in August.

Baumgardner said of Dubois to Sky Sports : "I just easily pick her apart. I see a lot of holes in her game. I see a lot of her questioning herself and how she does things.

"I don't need a trainer to tell me step-by-step what to do. I already know it because I see it.

"She knows deep down that she's up for a challenge. She's hungry, she's a champion but she knows that she's up against a world-class fighter.

"She knows that she's going to really have to up her game, but every time she ups her game, I up mine 10 more, so you're trying to reach something that you can't fully reach.

"When that time comes, we'll see. A fight against Caroline is definitely there but she still needs to do her job. She still needs to show up."

'Nur Turhan has never been in the ring with someone like me'

Baumgardner, whose 18-1 CV features wins over Mikaela Mayer and, most recently, Bo Mi Re Shin, labelled Nur Turhan a "one-way fighter" and expects her opponent to struggle from the off this weekend.

Nur Turhan snatched the IBF lightweight title with a fifth-round knockout of Beatriz Ferreira in December 2025 having also floored the Brazilian in the first round.

Baumgardner added of Nur Turhan: "I wouldn't say she is the most dangerous [fighter I have faced] but she does hit hard.

"I haven't felt her power enough to know if she hits hard [but] in terms of how she beat a world champion like Beatriz [Ferreira], I have to give her credit for that.

"She has never been in the ring with someone like me. I am not just a one-way fighter like herself: I have skills, I have great power, I have great footwork and my timing is impeccable. Skills pay the bills.

"The previous fights I have seen she is easy to hit. Once she gets hit by my power she is going to realise, 'okay, I've got to either throw hard or find a way out of here'."

Assessing the prospect of becoming a two-weight world champion, Baumgardner said: "It would just build the résumé. With women's boxing, we have to look at who people are fighting and the reasoning.

"I am stepping up and fighting a fighter no one in the 135lb division wanted to fight. That tells a story and adds to my résumé that I'm always up for the challenge.

"Not only that, I'm fighting three-minute rounds. I keep setting the standard for myself and who Alycia Baumgardner is."

Asked whether she is ready to take the mantle of the No 1 in women's boxing following Katie Taylor's retirement, the 32-year-old added: "I already took it. They didn't have to give it to me. I took the torch, I didn't need it to be passed down.

"I'm going to continue doing what I'm doing and that's what I'm showcasing on November 8.

"Viewers can see an impactful fight first off. It's going to be a lot of details in there but the knockout is coming."

Watch Elif Nur Turhan vs Alycia Baumgardner for the IBF lightweight title live on Sky Sports+ on Monday morning, with the card starting from 1.30am. Latest Sky Sports deals or stream with NOW.

articles.title: Cheavon Clarke rejects Chris Billam-Smith handshake at face-off ahead of Saturday's fight at Copper Box Arena
articles.summary: Chris Billam-Smith fights Cheavon Clarke in the headline event of Zuffa Boxing 12 at the Copper Box Arena on Saturday; Denzel Bentley meets Shane Mosley Jr with Da'Mazion Vanhouter and Sam Hickey in action; Watch Zuffa Boxing 12 on Saturday live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
Billam-Smith has made it clear he has a score to settle with Clarke after a painful amateur defeat in the final of the elite championships a decade ago.

They now box as professionals, headlining the Zuffa Boxing 12 event this weekend in London.

They addressed each other directly as they stated their case for victory. Clarke eventually allowed a fist bump, but wasn't willing to shake hands with the former world champion and they both stared each other out for a protracted amount of time.

Clarke beat Billam-Smith in the 2016 amateur championship final before both went on to an assessment for the GB squad. It was Clarke who progressed to the international team and ultimately the Olympic Games.

"I never stole his place. We fought, I won on the day and we both had the opportunity," Clarke said.

He did though expect, eventually, to fight Billam-Smith again as a pro. "Of course, you're going to meet at some point if you're trying to elevate yourself," Clarke said.

Billam-Smith did go on to excel as a professional, winning the WBO world title when he upset Lawrence Okolie in 2023.

He actually believes he might never have become a world champion if hadn't lost that amateur bout to Clarke.

"I probably never would have ended up training with Shane [McGuigan]. Shane is genuinely the only coach out there that would have got the best out of me," Billam-Smith said.

Clarke impressed in his last fight, when he rose from the canvas twice to stop Jack Massey. But Billam-Smith is convinced he wouldn't have let Clarke off the hook.

"If I had Chev hurt I believe I can get rid of him," Billam-Smith said. "I believe I can hurt any cruiserweight in the world and I can get rid of any cruiserweight in the world."

But his opponent warned: "I'm Cheavon Clarke, you can't ever count me out."

Watch Billam-Smith vs Clarke on Saturday live on Sky Sports.

articles.title: Alycia Baumgardner Talks Claressa Shields Rivalry, Next Fight with MVP and More in B/R Interview
articles.summary: Before she attempts to become a two-division world champion on Sunday night, Alycia Baumgardner has put her rivalry with Claressa Shields firmly behind her.
articles.body:
Before she attempts to become a two-division world champion on Sunday night, Alycia Baumgardner has put her rivalry with Claressa Shields firmly behind her.

Following a backstage altercation in May that resulted in Shields being banned from all Most Valuable Promotions events, Baumgardner said she's leveled up to new challenges.

"I'm doing my thing. She's doing her thing. And that's that. … I have so much bigger fights to entertain than her," Baumgardner told Bleacher Report. "Again, I'm in my own lane doing my own thing, creating my own stage, and she can't even fit. I don't even see her fitting on that type of stage with me."

Most Likely Heel, Face Turns at WWE Crown Jewel 2026

Predicting Next Year's Crown Jewel Matches 🔮

That level of confidence is why the unified junior lightweight champion already adamantly feels like she is the face of women's boxing, even before she challenges IBF lightweight champion Elif Nur Turhan in the main event of MVPW-07 on ESPN on Sunday night.

"What makes me the face of women's boxing already is what I'm doing and how I'm doing things," Baumgardner said. "I came into this game as the underdog, and I still feel like I'm that underdog. I'm setting the stage of fighting three minutes. I'm setting the stage of bringing hooks and looks to the stage, the beauty and the beast, the femininity. I am the weigh-in. People look forward to Alycia Baumgardner's weigh-in. When it comes to my hairstyle, the heart that you see everybody wearing, AB started that. Alycia Bumgartner started that. Coming with the fashion, high fashion, I started that. That's who I am, my identity and what I'm shaping to show women that you can be a beauty and a beast, and when it's time to do what you gotta do, you can do that."

Unbeaten since 2019, Baumgardner (18-1, 7 KOs) is setting a new precedent by fighting under men's rules with three-minute rounds. Her fight against Turhan will be contested in 10 three-minute rounds, and she previously fought under 12-round men's championship rules in the co-main event of Netflix's Jake Paul vs. Anthony Joshua fight card last December, becoming just the second female unified champion in history to defend her titles under those rules.

"For me, it's important because I love the challenge. I love that this is something that I'm able to do. This is something that I'm able to set a standard for myself. And again, this builds my resume. So when we go back and we talk about Alycia, why was she so good? Or what did she do different than some? She stepped up to the plate," Baumgardner said. "... This next fight is three minutes once again, and I also think it fits my style. To have to rush in two minutes is a bit annoying, so three minutes really breaks down the fighter. And I'm a fighter with skills, I have a toolbox, and so it's nice that I can break down a fighter. Just as if you were watching a men's match, you see how they break them down and how they build to get that knockout. And so that's what I'm doing."

However, the 32-year-old admitted that she doesn't see three-minute rounds becoming the norm in women's boxing anytime soon, because not everyone is built like her.

"It's a great question. It's not a standard for everybody, I have to say that. Not everybody can fight three minutes, I don't expect people to. But this is what I'm doing, and this is what I'm doing to set myself apart," she said. "And that's what's nice about boxing is that you don't have to be like everybody else, you can set yourself apart. And that's what I've done my whole career and continue to do, to set the stage for myself."

Despite being undersized against Turhan, Baumgardner's confidence level remains high. While she isn't overlooking her opponent, she feels she will be the faster and more polished fighter when they meet in the ring.

"I've accomplished everything that I wanted at 130 [pounds]," Baumgardner said. "And as a businesswoman, this was the best business move to do. And so moving up to cement my legacy, my resume, who I am as a fighter, this fight will show why I'm the face.

"The only challenge that I see is that she's wild," she added about Turhan. "I have to make sure that I'm going to protect myself as well. It's easy to get hit behind the head and those types of things because she has no fundamentals. So I have to make sure that I'm sharp, I'm composed, I'm using the ring, I'm punching in between her punches, and every time she misses, she will pay."

As for how far up she'd like to move, Baumgardner said she could see herself conquering another weight class and becoming a three-division world champion.

"You know, I wouldn't mind to move up to 140. I think 140 would be the next weight class," she said. "I'm focusing on 135, but I think 140 could be the next one."

Baumgardner will be looking for her first finish since 2021, and she has a simple prediction for how Sunday's fight against Turhan will end.

"My prediction is a knockout," she said.

articles.title: Buatsi vs Hutchinson 2: Scottish light-heavyweight dreams of winning WBC world championship
articles.summary: Scotland's Willy Hutchinson is out to realise the dream he wrote about as a 13-year-old when he fights Joshua Buatsi for the vacant WBC light-heavyweight title this weekend.
articles.body:
Scotland's Willy Hutchinson will be on a mission to realise the dream he wrote about as a 13-year-old when he fights for the vacant WBC light-heavyweight title on Saturday.

Hutchinson and British rival Joshua Buatsi meet in a rematch at Manchester's AO Arena, just over two years after Buatsi earned a split-decision win in a thrilling first contest.

At the final news conference before the championship fight, Hutchinson, 28, explained that he jotted down his boxing goals as a teenager while working with his dad - and becoming WBC champion was at the top.

After David Benavidez gave up the WBC gold to move up to cruiserweight, a fight that was originally scheduled to be for the interim title was upgraded.

"I wrote on a pen and book that I'll become Scottish, British, European and world amateur champion," Hutchinson said.

"On the opposite side of this book - I'm 13 and I still have this book to this day - I wrote that I'll become WBC champion of the world.

"I already got the silver and the international and now I'm fighting for the main belt."

The 'Hutch-Train' became the first Scottish boxer to win gold at an amateur World Championships nearly 10 years ago, triumphing at youth level.

The date of that victory and the Buatsi fight night are just days apart on the calendar, which Hutchinson says is "absolutely fantastic".

Broadcaster Adam Smith, who hosted Thursday's news conference, challenged Hutchinson to bring along the book containing his boxing ambitions on Saturday night and the Scot said he was "sure we can sort something".

Hutchinson managed to get under Buatsi's skin during the build-up to the first fight, but there was no sign of that this time as they spoke at Manchester's New Century Hall.

The fighters were asked about their newfound respect for each other, with Hutchinson saying he's "had to mature".

The Scot did edge ever closer to Buatsi during the face-off, and the tension could be felt, but that maturity remained intact.

Hutchinson finding happiness after emotional turmoil

Winning titles 'wasn't a dream' for Buatsi

Unlike his opponent, Buatsi had no designs on becoming a boxing star as a youngster.

"My life was very different to all of this. Fighting in arenas, winning titles and going to the Olympics, as a little boy, this wasn't a dream of mine," Buatsi said.

The Londoner, now 33, was tipped for great things when he claimed an Olympic bronze medal at the 2016 Rio Games, but his progress has been slower than expected.

With a record of 20 wins and one defeat as a professional, this is potentially Buatsi's only chance of winning a world title.

He looked relaxed throughout the news conference and mingled with the media afterwards.

"When I started the sport, I got off to winning ways, carried on, and then the dream came," Buatsi said.

"As a little boy, if you asked if I wanted to do this, hell no.

"I didn't have the vision for it, but now I've had it, we've tuned in on it, and we're almost there."

articles.title: Denzel Bentley reveals job snub before becoming world middleweight champion as he prepares to face Shane Mosley Jr
articles.summary: Denzel Bentley takes on Shane Mosley Jr in a top-class middleweight clash this Saturday at the Copper Box Arena; Bentley has been stripped of his world title outside the ring, but takes confidence from how he's overcome adversity before; watch Bentley vs Mosley live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
The Battersea fighter is smarting from the WBO stripping him of his hard-won middleweight world title, but has to focus on a dangerous bout with Shane Mosley Jr on Saturday, live on Sky Sports .

Bentley fights Mosley Jr on the Zuffa Boxing 12 bill, headlined by Chris Billam-Smith vs Cheavon Clarke .

The WBO required Bentley to box his mandatory challenger, Yoenli Hernandez next. It was a fight Bentley was willing to take, but he had committed to fighting Mosley Jr , which he wanted to do as a voluntary defence or even a non-title bout.

"We put up a really good case and everything we mentioned was kind of ignored," Bentley told Sky Sports . "The reasons as to why they stripped me are their reasons.

"[WBC middleweight champion Carlos] Adames is able to do a non-title fight and box.

"I was happy to fight Hernandez next year," he added. "They just want to seem like they're doing justice, but they're not."

The son of boxing legend Shane Mosley, Junior is coming off a tremendous stoppage victory over Serhii Bohachuk. He is also rated No 6 in the WBO's own rankings.

"If this was for a world title, everyone would be like this is a good defence. He's No 6 with the WBO, everyone knows his resume, he's fought top fighters and I'd say he deserves a title shot if I'm being honest," Bentley said.

"I deserve to defend my title. I'm being criticised for my move but that's because a lot of people out there are putting out narratives to try and take a hit on Zuffa as a promotional company. I'm just in the middle of the crossfire.

"It's not [fair] but life is not fair. You've just got to take it as it is."

Bentley has vowed to use all this antagonism to fuel his motivation for Saturday's fight.

"I'm expecting a dogfight at some point, it should be good. I get excited about these fighters. He's a good fighter and if I turn up I can put on a good performance," he said.

"I'm free of all this circus and I can just move forward and box like I want to do."

Bentley has overcome setbacks in life and career before. He has faced adversity becoming a three-time British middleweight champion. He lost his first world title fight, but came back eventually to win the WBO's interim belt that was upgraded to the full world championship.

He was out of action for more than a year before his crucial fight with Endry Saavedra that saw him secure the interim strap. That was a struggle. He was looking for work outside of the sport, but could not even get jobs as a delivery driver.

"I was out for 16 months," Bentley said. "During that time there was no income because I wasn't fighting.

"It's hard for boxers to get sponsors and I just couldn't get anything going so I was trying to apply for Amazon delivery, like a zero-hour contract one, you just download the app put in your details and it just gives you jobs and you just do it whenever you can.

"And there were just no jobs in my area at the time. That's the only reason why I didn't do it.

"I just couldn't get any work. I just had to sit tight and wait for a fight date.

"I don't think I take enough time to sit back and think about my journey. When you put it like that it is quite incredible."

Watch Bentley vs Mosley Jr this Saturday live on Sky Sports .

articles.title: Tyson Fury camp deny injury claims ahead of The Gypsy King's fight with Anthony Joshua in Cardiff
articles.summary: Former British heavyweight boxer Frank Bruno has claimed Tyson Fury could be injured, which 'The Gypsy King's' camp have denied; watch Zuffa Boxing 12, featuring Chris Billam-Smith vs Cheavon Clarke, on Saturday at 7pm, live on Sky Sports+
articles.body:
Fury and Joshua will finally face each other on December 11 in Cardiff for the WBA (Super) heavyweight title after years of back and forth.

However, former British heavyweight boxer Frank Bruno has cast doubt on the fight and suggested Fury could be injured.

"I looked at him the other day and I think someone was talking to me in the gym that he's got some injury, which may stop him from going into the fight with Anthony Joshua? And having that on your head ain't nice," said Bruno on the Fight Your Corner podcast.

Fury's camp have denied the claim to Sky Sports News , so the Fury-Joshua fight is set to go ahead as scheduled.

The fight is due to begin at around 1am in the early hours of Saturday December 12, with the Principality Stadium remaining open until 3.30am.

Last week, Fury said he intends to carry on boxing after December's blockbuster clash, even though at 38 he is at a late stage in his career.

"I'm going to continue. I've got two fights left on my contract. I'll finish the contract off and then probably sign another 10-fight deal. Who knows?" he said when speaking to WSVN Miami from his training camp.

"If the money's right sign another 10 fights, but they've got to be quick because I'm getting older. And when it's gone it's gone. I'm coming up to fight No 40."

articles.title: Conor Benn reveals that he could fight boxing legend Manny Pacquiao early next year: 'We can do it, no problem'
articles.summary: Conor Benn reveals he was offered a December fight with Manny Pacquiao; he could not be ready for that but believes talks can be restarted for the fight in the first quarter of 2027; watch Chris Billam-Smith vs Cheavon Clarke on Saturday live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
Benn revealed to Sky Sports that he had been offered a December bout with Pacquiao.

But after the rigours of making welterweight and suffering a stoppage loss to Ryan Garcia in Las Vegas in September, he wasn't able to box Pacquiao next month.

He hopes though to restart talks to have the fight with Pacquiao in the first quarter of 2027.

"He's an all-time legend. He's an eight-division world champion, he's an all-time, he'll go down in the history books," Benn told Sky Sports , before adding: "Another stadium show sounds nice.

"I know the Pacquiao fight was offered to me for December. And I wasn't ready to get the fight done in December. But if he wants it Q1 next year, we can do Pacquiao," he revealed.

"The fight got presented to me for December and it was just too soon, making weight, got a newborn son, so for me it was really about spending time with my family."

But he added: "If Q1, he wants to get it on again, I'm interested.

"Always in the gym, always working, if he wants it Q1 next year, we can do it, no problem."

Garcia, the WBC welterweight champion, stopped Benn inside two rounds in the Briton's first world title challenge. "It's a hard pill to swallow," Benn acknowledged.

"To give 100 per cent in everything I do, I always want to be victorious. No one likes losing. You always want to come first place. So for me it's just one of those things, you go swimming, you get wet. And I always said I want to be in exciting fights and if I get caught, I get caught."

Garcia dropped him heavily though Benn was back on his feet when the stoppage came. He did not however criticise the referee for ending the fight.

"It's hard to say. I mean, listen I respect the referee and it's the referee's job to keep the fighter safe," he said.

"Obviously me knowing my style and who I am, would I have liked to let the fight carry on, of course, but I'm not going to argue with the referee, he was there to do his job and he did his job.

"If he didn't think I was fit to continue that was his call on the night. Ultimately, as I say, you swimming you get wet. You keep it moving."

He however won't fight at welterweight again. "I don't know what I was thinking making 147lbs. You think right now I'm 185, 186lbs," he noted.

"Making 147, a lot of people said I can't do it and of course the inner me was: 'Alright cool, you can't do it - watch me.' It's one thing making the weight and it's one thing performing at your best at the weight. And you know it showed, I paid the price for chasing greatness.

"My future's at middleweight. I thought about light-middle, there's nothing in me at light-middle either - that's how bad the weight cut was.

"There's no excuses, Ryan is a phenomenal fighter, caught me with a phenomenal shot and he was the better man on the night.

"I dust it all off, dust the cobwebs off and come back and be a better version of myself."

articles.title: Topuria rompe su silencio tras caer ante Gaethje: "Podía pensar hasta en retirarme"
articles.standfirst: El hispanogeorgiano concede a ABC su primera entrevista desde que perdió el cinturón del peso ligero de la UFC y su condición de invicto en la Casa Blanca
articles.summary: El hispanogeorgiano concede a ABC su primera entrevista desde que perdió el cinturón del peso ligero de la UFC y su condición de invicto en la Casa Blanca
articles.body: Ilia Topuria llevaba casi cinco meses sin hablar de la derrota que cambió su carrera. El 14 de junio, Justin Gaethje le arrebató el cinturón del peso ligero de la UFC y acabó con su invicto en el combate estelar de la velada celebrada en la Casa Blanca. Ahora, en una entrevista concedida a ABC en Tiflis, el hispanogeorgiano admite que había llegado a contemplar la retirada y cuenta cómo aquella derrota cambió su manera de mirar al futuro. "Soy una persona que siempre va a seguir adelante, una persona que jamás se va a rendir. Esto ha cambiado todo. Había exprimido todo ya, podía pensar hasta en retirarme", afirma en el adelanto publicado por el diario. El Matador sostiene que todavía le queda un gran combate por delante. "La pelea más grande en la UFC ahora lleva mi nombre y apellido", asegura. En ese adelanto, Topuria deja en el aire quién sería su rival. Topuria había llegado como favorito al combate más mediático de su carrera, disputado ante Donald Trump con motivo del 80º cumpleaños del presidente estadounidense. Gaethje dio la sorpresa y le infligió su primera derrota como profesional.

articles.title: Ilia Topuria Targets Paddy Pimblett for April 2027 Return, Admits Retirement Is on His Mind
articles.summary: Ilia Topuria discusses his return plans, targets Paddy Pimblett for April 2027, and hints at retirement in his first interview since UFC Freedom 250.
articles.body:
Now that Ilia Topuria is back in training and targeting an early 2027 UFC return, fans can already start imagining him finally settling his long-standing rivalry with Paddy Pimblett.

The bad blood between the two dates back to UFC London in 2022 , when they clashed during the event's press conference and even threw bottles at each other at their hotel. Pimblett later trolled Topuria by pretending to purchase the red-corner stool used during the June 14 event for nearly $14,000 , although the entire story was, of course, made up.

The Englishman even proposed settling their rivalry through a season of The Ultimate Fighter to build more hype around the matchup. Dana White was also happy to entertain the idea, suggesting that the fight could headline a numbered UFC event without a title on the line.

And it seems Topuria is on the same page. In his first exclusive interview since UFC Freedom 250, a preview clip released by ABC Diario on Thursday showed the former two-division champion calling out Pimblett while discussing his future inside the Octagon.

Along with opening up about the psychological impact of his loss to Justin Gaethje, Topuria also addressed the possibility of retiring after his next fight. He said, "I've achieved everything, and after this fight, what else?" Maybe I'll even retire."

However, before potentially walking away from the sport, he has one rivalry he wants to settle. Topuria pitched April 2027 as a possible return date and made it clear that Pimblett is the opponent he wants. He said, "Like you have never seen him before. From April onward is when we are considering returning. I have always been aware that in this life, not everything is a bed of roses, even though I've never had it before."

He then had a message specifically for his longtime rival, saying, "Paddy, Paddy, Paddy. I'll eat him like a sausage, which he is."

If Topuria can return and beat Pimblett in his comeback fight, it would put him in a strong position to work his way back toward the UFC lightweight title by the end of 2027. However, the division is already crowded, with Gaethje's future still uncertain and contenders like Arman Tsarukyan and Alexander Volkanovski also eyeing 155-pound gold.

Still, given the history between Topuria and Pimblett, this is one rivalry the UFC would have a hard time ignoring.
